gap: No result ChatGPT got states the cost per laptop watt or watts per ounce for TESSAN's WTA09. On tessan.com on 2026-11-13 it is $27.99 for 65 W on USB-C3, which works out to $0.43 per laptop watt, against $0.66 for the WTA07 and $0.71 to $0.77 for EPICKA's TA-105 Pro and Pulse Duo. It is also the heaviest of them at 7.18 oz, which gives 9.05 W/oz.
standout_why: Kit Authority (cited) already gives the WTA07's $42.99 price and 6.04 oz weight, so the WTA07 figures can be worked out from it, but it doesn't cover the WTA09. TreksSavvy gives the EPICKA Air 65W's weight (5.26 oz / 149 g) and says, citing the manual, that its laptop port drops to 40 W plus 15 W once another port is in use. So the most useful number here, the laptop watts left while a phone charges, is already on a rival page for the Air, and I couldn't source it for the TESSANs. MobilePlusTech has no prices, weights or splits for these models. I couldn't open WIRED (cited) because the fetch was blocked, so I don't know what it says. One ChatGPT answer already showed the WTA09 at $27.99. What is new is the per-watt and per-ounce math across all the candidates.
decides: It backs TESSAN's WTA09 as the value pick: it's the cheapest 65 W single-port option by a wide margin ($0.43/W against $0.66–$0.77/W). The cost is weight: at 7.18 oz it carries 9.05 W/oz, against 10.76 for the WTA07 and 12.4 for the EPICKA Air 65W. The Air stays the light pick, but per TreksSavvy its laptop port gives only 40 W while another port charges. For a shopper who needs 65 W to the laptop and a phone at the same time, none of the under-$50 models has a published figure that guarantees it.
